security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate integration documentation, but it handles sensitive wallet identity material, persistent agent configuration, sudo service control, and paid P2P inference routing. Most static URL, Markdown backtick, and placeholder API-key matches are false positives, but several findings are confirmed because they affect funds, secrets, or persistent routing. Static review was capped at 400/648 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 248 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Wallet identity and deposits are security-sensitive.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before generating, storing, printing, or reusing ANTSEED_IDENTITY_HEX or identity.key. Recommend small deposits and reserve caps.

remediation.issue: The skill changes persistent user-level agent configs.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before editing home-directory config files, back them up, and merge only the AntSeed provider block while preserving unrelated settings.

remediation.issue: Prompts and metadata are routed to third-party peers.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before routing private code, secrets, or regulated data through AntSeed peers. Confirm the selected peer and service id first.

remediation.issue: Some setup paths require elevated system commands.
remediation.suggestion: Do not run sudo commands automatically. Show the exact command and wait for explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Global package and GitHub extension installs add supply-chain risk.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted package versions where possible, verify source repositories, and ask before global installs or extension installs.

remediation.issue: Placeholder API keys can be confused with real secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder values clearly labeled, and never read, log, or overwrite existing .env secrets without user approval.

content.value_statement: AI tools need consistent proxy setup across many clients. This skill provides setup steps for routing Claude, Codex, SDKs, and HTTP clients through AntSeed.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to start and verify the AntSeed buyer proxy on localhost.
Shows setup paths for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, OpenClaw, and Hermes.
Provides SDK examples for Vercel AI SDK and LangChain clients.
Documents peer pinning, service discovery, protocol matching, and per-request peer headers.
Lists local AntSeed files used for identity, state, metering, payments, and plugins.
Includes troubleshooting steps for model selection, streaming, proxy reachability, and metering.
limitations: Requires the AntSeed desktop app or CLI buyer proxy to be running locally.
Requires a pinned peer or a per-request peer header before most calls work.
Paid services require USDC deposits on Base and may open payment channels.
The skill is documentation only and does not validate peer trust or model quality.

faq.question: Does this skill run AntSeed by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions. The user or agent must run the desktop app or CLI buyer proxy.

faq.question: Which clients are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, OpenClaw, Hermes, GenLayer Studio, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, and raw HTTP.

faq.question: Do I need a real OpenAI or Anthropic API key?
faq.answer: Usually no. Most examples use a placeholder key because AntSeed authenticates with the local buyer identity.

faq.question: Why do calls fail with no_peer_pinned?
faq.answer: The buyer proxy needs a session peer pin or a per-request peer header before it can route the request.

faq.question: Can AntSeed calls spend money?
faq.answer: Yes. Paid services use USDC deposits on Base and may open payment channels on first use.

faq.question: What should I protect most carefully?
faq.answer: Protect ANTSEED_IDENTITY_HEX and ~/.antseed/identity.key. They control the buyer identity and access to deposits.
